text:
deploy-bot: Starting config-only rollout 'tinyflow-route-2' (change window 22:00 PST). Changes: routing policy weight shift -> tinyflow, max_batch_size 8 -> 6, soft_timeout 2.5s -> 2.0s. Canary: 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 15m. Rolling back criteria: >3% absolute error increase or p95 > 500ms.

anya: ack, I'm watching metrics from the product side. Are we pinning any model versions with this?

mike: Not touching model binaries  config-only. We'll pin the routing policy id 'rp-tiny-2026-03' during the rollout. Fallback plan is to flip weights back to previous policy. Quick rollback API: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/routing/rollback 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN' 
  -d '{"policy_id":"rp-tiny-2026-03"}'
```

sean: Heads-up on signals: watch p95 token latency, kv-cache miss rate, request queue depth (>20 indicates backpressure). I'll push a temporary panel on the infra dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/in/d/infra/canary-playback

ops-runbot: Alert created: canary-error-rate (threshold=2.0%, window=5m) and canary-p95 (threshold=450ms, window=5m). Will post if thresholds hit.

anya: quick sanity: reducing max_batch_size should lower memory footprint but may raise per-request overhead. Confirm tenant-level rate caps are unchanged. Also keeping tenant floor=1 so tiny requests still served.

mike: Confirmed  tenant caps unchanged. Ramp plan: 5% -> 25% (30m) -> 60% (60m) -> 100% if healthy. Release notes draft: "Routing: introduce tinyflow policy with lower batch sizes and tightened soft timeout to reduce tail latency for low-variance workloads." I'll paste final after full ramp.

deploy-bot: Canary update: 15m complete. Metrics snapshot: canary-error-rate +0.4% (baseline 0.8% -> 1.2%), p95 +18ms, kv-cache-miss +0.7pp. No alerts fired. Proceeding to ramp to 25% now.

anya: :+1: I'll stay on-call for the 25% window and will trigger rollback if error climbs above 3% or p95 spikes beyond our threshold.

mike: thanks team  tagging @oncall for 60m window.

(End of thread)
